You're correct - `text-align` doesn't make sense for an icon. Since this is a `.weather-icon` with fixed dimensions (40px x 40px), the `text-align` property should be removed entirely. The icon positioning is already handled by the `vertical-align: middle` and the padding properties.


---

<tool-use data-tool-type="write" data-tool-name="search_replace">

<details><summary>Tool use: **search_replace** • Edit file: /Users/deg/Documents/basistech/temperature-bot/app/static/style.css</summary>

```diff
-     text-align: left;

      padding-left: 5px;
```

</details>

</tool-use>

---

Perfect! I've removed the inappropriate `text-align: left;` property from the `.weather-icon` class. 

For an icon element, the positioning is properly handled by:
- `vertical-align: middle` - aligns the icon vertically with surrounding text/content
- `padding-left: 5px` and `padding-right: 5px` - provides horizontal spacing
- The fixed `width: 40px` and `height: 40px` dimensions

The `text-align` property only affects text content within an element, not the element itself, so it was indeed inappropriate for an icon. The CSS is now cleaner and more semantically correct.
